_comment: What is actually deployed, per network. Checked against the ledger by scripts/verify-deployed-hashes.mjs (.github/workflows/deployed-hashes.yml). Deployed contracts cannot be upgraded, so these hashes change only when a new factory is deployed; contracts/expected-hashes.json tracks the current build and may legitimately differ.

names._comment: Veil Names registry. The wasm_sha256 here is the DEPLOYED artifact, built with `stellar contract build` for the wasm32v1-none target. It deliberately differs from contracts/expected-hashes.json, which records a plain `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` artifact: that one enables reference-types and Soroban's VM rejects it outright (WasmVm, InvalidAction). Two different builds of the same source, only one of which can be deployed.
names.ttl_note: Soroban entries archive when their TTL lapses. A name's TTL is bumped to 30 days on every read or write by the contract itself, so active names keep themselves alive. The contract's own wasm and instance are NOT self-renewing and need `stellar contract extend` roughly monthly, paid from the admin account, or the whole registry stops resolving.
